# FDG6022

> CONSIDER sealing members that you override.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 6.3 Sealing.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Library only: sealing an override shields the class from the problems of virtual members (section 6.1.4) for subclasses outside the library. Not an analyzer candidate: whether an override stays an extension point for further subclasses is a design decision; in the dispose pattern of section 9.4, for example, subclasses override Dispose(bool) again.

## From the book

```csharp
public class FlowSwitch : SourceSwitch {
  protected sealed override void OnValueChanged() {
    ...
  }
}
```

Problems that can result from introducing virtual members (discussed in section 6.1.4) apply to overrides as well, although to a slightly lesser degree. Sealing an override shields you from these problems starting from that point in the inheritance hierarchy.

In short, part of designing for extensibility is knowing when to limit it, and sealed types are one of the mechanisms by which you do that.
